newsitem.title: MALDIVES: One fifth of humanity lives in South Asia region.
newsitem.headline: One fifth of humanity lives in South Asia region.

text.p: The leaders of seven South Asian states meet in the Maldives this week to discuss strengthening cooperation within a region whose 1.2 billion people make up one fifth of the world's population.

The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) comprises the Himalayan kingdoms of Bhutan and Nepal, the Indian Ocean island nations of the Maldives and Sri Lanka, mostly Hindu India and its Moslem majority neighbours, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
Following are the names of the heads of state or government attending the three-day summit starting on Monday, and other key details:
BANGLADESH - Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Capital Dhaka. Population 115 million. Per capita gross national product (in 1993, Human Development Centre) $220.
BHUTAN - King Jigme Singye Wangchuk. Capital Thimphu. Population 675,000, mostly Buddhists. Per capita GNP $170. About 30-35 percent of the population in the south are ethnic Nepalese.

INDIA - Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral. Capital New Delhi. Population 960 million, mostly Hindu. Per capita GNP $300. Some 19 percent of the people live below the poverty line, unable to afford minimum adequate nutrition and non-food essentials.
MALDIVES - President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. Capital Male. Population 213,215, all Sunni Moslems. Per capita GNP $820.

NEPAL - Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand. Capital Kathmandu. Population 21 million. Per capita GNP $190. The world's only Hindu monarchy, Nepal maintained self-imposed isolation until the middle of this century.
PAKISTAN - Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. Capital Islamabad. Population 131.6 million. Per capita GNP $430. An Islamic nation, majority Sunni Moslems.

SRI LANKA - President Chandrika Kumaratunga. Capital Colombo. Population 18.2 million, mostly Buddhists. Per capita GNP $600. About 13 percent of the people are Tamils. Tamil separatists have been waging a war for independence in the north and east since 1983.
